what_it_does: Code hosting, pull requests, issues, Actions CI and repository collaboration.
auth_notes: OAuth via GitHub App or OAuth App; personal access tokens sent as Bearer. GitHub App JWT/installation tokens are standard but the REST auth page could not be opened this pass (MCP docs confirm OAuth + PAT).
access_notes: Free GitHub account can create PATs and register OAuth/GitHub Apps; not re-verified against docs.github.com this pass (fetch blocked).
api_notes: REST and GraphQL APIs covering repos, issues, PRs, Actions, code security, users, orgs. MCP toolsets (repos, issues, pull_requests, actions, code_security, users) reflect breadth.

what_it_does: Frontend cloud for deploying and hosting web apps and serverless functions.
auth_notes: Access tokens (account/team/project scoped, vcp_ prefix) sent as Bearer. Integrations use OAuth code exchange at api.vercel.com/v2/oauth/access_token; long-lived integration tokens deprecated in favor of 1-hour short-lived tokens via client_credentials.
access_notes: Any Vercel account can create access tokens on the Account Tokens page; Vercel MCP 'available on all plans'. Billing scope only on Pro/Enterprise. Public Marketplace listing of an integration may need review (not required for testing).
api_notes: Deployments, projects, env vars, domains/DNS/certs, registrar, teams, drains, edge config, checks, billing.

what_it_does: Web hosting and deployment platform with serverless functions and forms.
auth_notes: Personal access tokens sent as Bearer; OAuth2 apps registered under Applications > OAuth applications (authorize at app.netlify.com/authorize). SAML SSO teams deny PAT access by default.
access_notes: PATs and OAuth apps created in the Netlify UI; docs list no plan restriction for API access. Rate limits 500 req/min, deploys 3/min and 100/day.
api_notes: REST API at api.netlify.com/api/v1 with OpenAPI spec at open-api.netlify.com; sites, deploys, forms, DNS, etc. Official Go and JS clients.

what_it_does: CDN, DNS, security and edge compute (Workers, R2, D1) platform.
auth_notes: Scoped API tokens (user or account-owned) recommended; legacy Global API key also supported. Cloudflare API MCP server supports OAuth; general third-party OAuth app availability for the API not verified.
access_notes: API tokens created in dashboard; free plan API access is widely available but the fetched page did not state plan coverage.
api_notes: Single REST API covering zones, DNS, Workers, R2, D1, WAF, Zero Trust and more; MCP server covers the full API.

what_it_does: Postgres backend platform with auth, storage, edge functions and realtime.
auth_notes: Management API: PAT as Bearer or OAuth app created in a Supabase org (both referenced in MCP docs). Per-project data APIs use project anon/service keys (not verified this pass).
access_notes: Self-serve signup; PATs and org OAuth apps created by the user. Free plan existence not re-verified on a pricing page this pass.
api_notes: Management API (projects, SQL, branches, functions, secrets) plus per-project auto-generated REST (PostgREST); Management API reference page could not be opened this pass.

what_it_does: Graph database (AuraDB cloud) queried with Cypher.
auth_notes: Two APIs: Aura API (instance management) uses OAuth2 client credentials -> 1-hour Bearer from api.neo4j.io/oauth/token. Query API (run Cypher over HTTPS at <dbid>.databases.neo4j.io, port 443) uses database credentials; Basic auth inferred, not confirmed on fetched page.
access_notes: Aura docs: 'All tiers can create Aura API credentials' (includes Free). Query API has no rate limit on Aura. For data tools use the Query API; Aura API only provisions/scales instances.
api_notes: Aura API: instances, tenants, snapshots. Query API: single Cypher endpoint (+ explicit transactions) giving full data access.

what_it_does: Cloud data warehouse and AI data platform.
auth_notes: REST/SQL APIs accept key-pair JWT, Snowflake or External OAuth, programmatic access tokens (PAT, Bearer), and workload identity federation. Per-account base URL.
access_notes: 30-day trial (or until free usage balance exhausted), email only, no card. AI/Cortex features disabled until a card is added; external network access, hybrid tables, Openflow unavailable on trial. Paid account needed after trial.
api_notes: SQL API plus Snowflake REST APIs for databases, schemas, warehouses, tables, users, roles, Cortex.
human_needed: add credit card to enable Cortex/AI features on trial

auth_notes: Atlas Administration API: service account OAuth2 client credentials -> Bearer token, or legacy API keys via HTTP Digest. Org Owner role needed to create them; optional IP access list.
access_notes: Self-serve Atlas account/org; free-tier eligibility for Admin API not stated on fetched page. Admin API does not access cluster data; data reads/writes need DB user + driver/connection string.
api_notes: Admin API v2 at cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2 for projects, clusters, users, access lists, backups, MCP configs. No REST data plane confirmed.
main_blocker: data operations need driver, not REST

what_it_does: Observability platform for metrics, logs, traces, monitors and security.
auth_notes: DD-API-KEY header, plus DD-APPLICATION-KEY for most read/manage endpoints; site-specific base URL (US1/EU1/etc). OAuth clients referenced in docs (details unverified). MCP also accepts PAT/service access tokens.
access_notes: 14-day free trial, no credit card. After trial a paid plan is needed (free tier not mentioned on trial page).
api_notes: ~179 resource groups in API reference (monitors, dashboards, logs, metrics, incidents, workflows...).
human_needed: org admin must enable MCP Access for the remote MCP

what_it_does: Application error tracking and performance monitoring.
auth_notes: User auth tokens (Bearer) with scopes like org:read, project:read/write, team:read/write, event:write; remote MCP uses OAuth. Sentry API auth page and integration OAuth not opened this pass.
access_notes: Self-serve signup and user auth tokens; free Developer plan not re-verified this pass.
api_notes: REST API for orgs, projects, teams, issues, events, releases (breadth inferred; reference not opened).
